title: The economic calendar
desc: The releases that move markets, and how to size around them

cards.title: Big trade, big day
cards.situation: You hold a trade four times your normal size. The monthly jobs report comes out tomorrow at 8:30. What’s the risk?

options.text: Little: one report rarely moves much
options.feedback: Big reports often move markets within seconds, and nobody knows which way.

options.text: Price can jump sharply either way at 8:30
options.feedback: Nobody knows the number in advance, so price can jump either way. Your size decides how much it hurts.

options.text: None: trading pauses until it’s out
options.feedback: Trading doesn’t pause. Price can jump the second the number lands, and your size decides how much it hurts.

cards.work: If the market jumps 1% against you, you lose four times what you would on your normal size.

cards.title: Three dates that move markets
cards.text: An **[[economic-calendar|economic calendar]]** lists when key data comes out. Three releases matter most.

items.title: US jobs report
items.sub: Monthly · jobs added. More than expected can mean rates stay higher

items.title: Rate decision
items.sub: About every 6 weeks · the new rate

blocks.tip: Price often jumps when the number lands, then swings both ways.

cards.title: A release, minute by minute
cards.text: These are index futures on CPI day. The report lands at 8:30.

items.title: CPI day · 8:00 to 9:00
items.label: Index futures flat until 8:30, then a jump, a reversal and a settle

cards.foot: In those first minutes, spreads widen and stops can fill at worse prices.

cards.title: Don’t carry big size into big news
cards.text: A release can move price more in a minute than in a normal day. If you’re wrong, an oversized trade turns a small loss into a big one.

items.title: Cut size or stay out before them

cards.rule: No oversized positions into big releases.

cards.title: Spot the risky day
cards.q: You trade short-term. Which day this week carries the most event risk?

options.feedback: Factory orders is a low-impact release. Look for the release marked high.
Consumer confidence is medium impact. Another day has a high-impact release that can move the whole market.
CPI is a high-impact release that can move the whole market, so Wednesday at 8:30 carries the most event risk.
Weekly jobless claims matter, but CPI is a high-impact release that can move the whole market.

cards.title: Before the decision
cards.q: The rate decision is at 2 pm. You hold a large position with a stop. What’s the sensible move?

options.text: Add more to catch the move
options.feedback: More size makes a jump against you hurt more. Nobody knows which way the decision will move price.

options.text: Cut it to a size you can live with
options.feedback: A smaller size keeps a jump either way to a loss you can live with, and your stop stays in place.

options.text: Remove the stop so a spike can’t hit it
options.feedback: The stop is your protection, and you need it most when price jumps. Cut the size instead.
Decisions can surprise, and price can swing hard even on an expected one. Cut the size beforehand.

cards.headline: You know the market’s big days.
lines: Jobs, CPI and rate decisions move markets most.
Price can jump both ways around a release.
Check the calendar weekly. Size down before big news.
